raw_segments.text: In 1309, Ralph de Bourne, prior of St. Augustine's, Canterbury, gave a feast upon his installation
day, of which William Thorne has preserved not only the bill of fare but the prices of
In that feast were consumed, first, fifty-three quarters of wheat, which cost nineteen pounds
or seven shillings and tuppence a quarter, equal to about one in twenty shillings and
six pence of our present money, two dly, fifty-eight quarters of malt, which cost seventeen
pounds ten shillings or six shillings a quarter, equal to about eighteen shillings of our present
money, three dly, twenty quarters of oats, which cost four pounds or four shillings
a quarter, equal to about twelve shillings of our present money.
